title: Association of proton pump inhibitors with risk of dementia: a pharmacoepidemiological claims data analysis
authors: Gomm W, von Holt K, Thomé F, Broich K, Maier W, Fink A, et al.
population: Members of the German statutory health insurer AOK aged 75 years or older and free of dementia at baseline
funder: No funding statement in the article information; Additional Contributions state: 'No compensation was received by the Scientific Research Institute from a funding sponsor for the study.' Authors are affiliated with the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases and the Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices, Bonn.
result: Regular PPI users (at least one PPI prescription in each quarter of an 18-month interval; n = 2950) had a higher risk of incident dementia diagnosis than non-users (n = 70,729): HR 1.44 (95% CI 1.36 to 1.52), adjusted for age, sex, comorbidities and polypharmacy. Diagnoses were claims codes; 29,510 participants developed dementia. The authors cite mouse studies in which PPIs raised brain beta-amyloid and call for randomised trials.
